newsitem.title: CHINA: China says to inspect data gathering.
newsitem.headline: China says to inspect data gathering.

text.p: China will begin an investigation of its statistical gathering this month in a bid to halt a flow of sometimes wildly inaccurate data.

"The move is aimed at curbing and correcting the illegal practice of putting out (intentionally) incorrect economic figures," the official China Daily on Friday quoted Vice-Premier Zou Jiahua as saying.
China has long had problems with the reliability of its economic data, often due to officials changing statistics to improve their performance in the eyes of their supervisors and the public.
Data has improved in recent years, however, as the shift to a market economy has increased the reliance of economic managers on valid data.
The latest probe follows similar reviews in 1989 and 1994 aimed at rooting out fraudulent data.
The 1994 inspection uncovered more than 60,000 cases of corrupt officials and company executives who tampered with economic statistics, the newspaper said.
The inspection will be conducted by the State Statistical Bureau, the Ministry of Supervision and the Legislative Affairs Bureau under the State Council (cabinet).
